NoMore® Colds
I've recommended sinus surgery to over three hundred patients in my career.

And for years, I believed it was the right thing to do.

Open up the blocked passages, and the symptoms go away. That's what every ENT is taught.

But after enough years in practice, something started to bother me.

Patients I operated on would come back months later—still unable to breathe clearly, still waking up congested, still living on steroid sprays.

The CT scans looked better. The suffering didn't.

And no one could explain why.

I remember one patient clearly.

A middle-aged mother of two named Jennifer. She'd spent seven years battling chronic sinusitis, trying every medication, every rinse, every specialist in town.

She came to me completely blocked. Constant facial pressure. Classic surgical candidate.

We did the procedure. It went smoothly.

Eight weeks later she came back and said, "I still can't breathe through my nose. I thought this would fix it."

I told her to give it time. That post-surgical swelling can take months to fully resolve.

Four months later, she said she still felt the same crushing pressure behind her eyes every morning.

That was the day I started questioning everything I thought I knew.

If blockage was the real cause, surgery should fix everyone.

But it didn't.

So why did so many people keep suffering even after we made "more space"?

That question kept me up at night.

I started reading every new study I could find.

Late nights at my desk. Cold coffee beside my notes. The same thought repeating in my head: What are we missing?

Then I found it.

It was a research paper from a European respiratory institute.

It said, "Chronic sinusitis is an inflammatory cycle where persistent swelling blocks drainage pathways, trapping mucus and irritants that feed continuous inflammation independent of the initial trigger."

I read it three times.

The real issue wasn't just blockage.

It was inflammation that never stops.

Years of constant swelling pinch shut those tiny drainage openings. The mucus can't escape. It sits there, stagnant, keeping the inflammation alive.

So even if you open the passages surgically, the tissues keep swelling shut again.

It finally made sense.

We'd been opening the doors but not putting out the fire inside the house.

Once I understood that, I started searching for ways to calm the inflammation safely.

Something noninvasive that could help the tissues heal naturally.

That's when a colleague—a researcher who'd been studying wound healing—told me about something NASA had been using for astronauts.

He said, "It's not a spray or a pill. It's light."

At first I laughed.

But then he showed me the research.

Red light therapy. Proven to reduce inflammation, decrease swelling, and help tissues repair themselves—the exact process that gets stuck in chronic sinusitis.

It wasn't heat. It wasn't medication. It was energy that encouraged the body to heal itself.

That got my attention.

I started reading every clinical study I could find on photobiomodulation for respiratory tissues.

The results were consistent.

Reduced inflammation. Decreased swelling. Faster mucosal healing.

It was the exact opposite of surgery.

Instead of cutting tissue to create space, it helped the tissue calm down from the inside out.

But I ran into one problem—every device I found was made for skin conditions or full-body panels. Nothing targeted the nasal passages where the inflammatory cycle lives.

Until a few months later, when that same researcher sent me a link and said, "You'll want to see this."

That's how I found NoMore.

A small company started by a group of biomedical engineers and former chronic sinusitis sufferers who had lived this problem firsthand.

One of the founders had been scheduled for his third sinus surgery, only to still wake up every morning feeling like his head was underwater.

They spent two years developing a device that could deliver medical-grade red light directly into the nasal passages—safely, effectively, and at home.

They called it the NoMoreColds Light Therapy Device.

It used the exact same 660nm red wavelengths used in clinical settings, but in a compact wand design that fits precisely where the inflammatory cycle occurs.

For the first time, it wasn't just another generic light therapy gadget.

It was designed specifically for chronic sinusitis patients.

And it was built to solve the same problem I'd been wrestling with for years—how to break the inflammatory cycle without surgery.

So I tried it myself.

As an ENT, I'd dealt with my own sinus issues for years. Decades of examining patients in dry clinic air had left my passages chronically irritated.

I inserted the device into my nostril, pressed the button, and watched the soft red glow through my skin.

6 minutes later, it shut off automatically.

It wasn't uncomfortable or hot—just a gentle warmth that seemed to reach deeper than surface tissue.

I used it every morning for three weeks.

By the end of that time, my morning congestion was nearly gone. I could breathe clearly through both nostrils. The pressure behind my cheekbones disappeared.

I couldn't ignore that.

So I started recommending it to a few of my patients who were trying to avoid surgery.

One of them, a high school teacher, came back after two weeks and said, "Doc, I can finally sleep without waking up choking on drainage."

Another told me she could smell her coffee again for the first time in four years.

That's when I realized this wasn't a coincidence.

When you give the body what it needs—reduced inflammation, open drainage pathways—it knows how to heal.

We just have to stop getting in the way.

I still perform surgery when it's absolutely necessary. But I don't rush into it anymore.

You can't cut your way to sinus health. You have to calm the inflammation.

That's why I recommend NoMoreColds. Not because it's flashy, but because it addresses what's actually happening inside your sinuses.

It helps calm the inflamed tissue, reduce the swelling, and break the cycle that keeps your sinuses blocked.

And when you do that, the body remembers how to heal.

I'm not sharing this as a sales pitch.

I've just seen too many people go under the knife without ever hearing this explanation.

If you're someone who's been told surgery is the only option, please, take a step back.

Learn what's really going on inside your sinuses before you make that decision.

For me, this discovery changed the way I practice medicine.

For my patients, it changed their lives.

And for you, it might be the thing that keeps you out of the operating room.

Here's the link to check it out if you're curious: https://try-nomore.com/pages/listicle-1-nomorecolds

No pressure.

Just information I wish every patient had before they let someone cut into their face.

Sometimes healing doesn't come from the scalpel.

Sometimes, it comes from light.

A client came to us frustrated — his website had been attacked multiple times, causing damage to his search rankings and leaving his customers with a broken, untrustworthy experience. His previous agency had assured him everything was "fine." It clearly wasn't.

When he reached out to us, we didn't guess. We audited.

What we found was exactly what these slides describe — the website had been built using AI tools with manual integrations stitched on top (hosting, plugins, third-party scripts). It looked functional. But underneath? Loopholes that were practically an open invitation.

We put together a detailed report. His reaction? Genuine shock — not because the damage was done, but because no one had ever looked this closely before.

We now manage his website along with a full suite of digital services. And he sleeps better at night.

I'm sharing this because every single day I hear the same narrative — "AI can build a website in 2 days, why would I pay an agency?"

And I want to be honest here, not defensive: AI has genuinely improved efficiency. I use it. My team uses it. It's a powerful tool.

But a tool is only as good as the hands holding it.

AI predicts code. It doesn't audit your security posture. It doesn't understand your business logic. It doesn't catch what it confidently generates wrong — and it won't be accountable when your site goes down or your customer data is compromised.

Speed is not safety. A fast launch without proper review isn't a launch — it's a liability.

What's your experience? Have you seen this play out firsthand? I'd love to hear from developers, founders, and business owners alike.

Every Parent Needs This!
I'm the mom who didn't check until it was too late. Three hotels, three cameras, all recording my daughter.

This was supposed to be Emma's perfect thirteenth birthday - four nights at Disney World.

By night three, we'd found cameras at three different hotels.

Friday we checked into a five-star resort right near Magic Kingdom with three thousand positive reviews. Emma got her birthday button at the front desk and wore it all weekend.

Saturday we did the parks and came back exhausted around 9 PM. Emma showered and fell asleep so happy, and I remember thinking I'd given her the perfect birthday.

Sunday morning I went to brush my teeth and the bathroom was still humid from Emma's shower the night before.

I noticed the air freshener plugged into the outlet next to the mirror - the holes in the front grill looked off, not quite even.

I unplugged it and turned it over in my hands, and the back had tiny screws. I used my nail file to unscrew one and the casing popped open.

Camera - small circuit board, lens, SD card slot, battery pack.

I sat down hard on the bathroom floor and just stared at it, my hands shaking so badly I almost dropped it.

Emma had showered in here last night, right here, while this thing recorded her.

Someone had video of my thirteen-year-old daughter naked on her birthday.

I couldn't breathe, just sat there on the cold tile trying not to throw up.

Hotel security came within fifteen minutes and police came thirty minutes after that. They took the camera and the SD card, told us they'd investigate, and asked questions about when we checked in, what time Emma had showered, and who had access to our room.

We packed everything and left immediately. Emma was crying and asking why someone would ever do this, and I didn't have an answer - I just kept saying we were going somewhere safe.

Sunday night we checked into a completely different hotel - different brand, different area, four miles away from the first one.

I went into the bathroom first and checked everything, unplugged the air freshener, checked behind the mirror, looked at the smoke detector, felt under the sink - nothing.

The room felt clean.

Emma showered and I stood outside the door the entire time, then she went to bed around 10 PM and I sat in the chair next to her for an hour watching her sleep.

She said she felt safer here.

Monday morning around 7 AM she woke me up, standing next to my bed crying and holding the alarm clock from her nightstand. Her hands were shaking.

"Mom, look at this."

The back panel was loose - she'd woken up and noticed it wasn't flush against the rest of the clock, so she pulled it off to see why. Camera inside, lens pointing directly at her bed through a small hole in the speaker grill.

She'd slept there for eight hours and changed out of her pajamas in the morning. Changed into her swimsuit to go to the pool - someone had recorded all of it.

Emma sat on the edge of the bed and just shook, not crying anymore, just shaking and staring at the camera in her hands. I tried to take it from her but she wouldn't let go, just kept staring at it.

"They watched me sleep, they watched me get dressed - Mom, they watched me."

We left without checking out, didn't even talk to the front desk, just grabbed our bags and threw them in the car. Emma sat in the back seat the entire drive and didn't say a word, just stared out the window.

I found a third hotel with availability and checked in Monday afternoon, but this time I didn't wait.

Before I even brought Emma inside, I went to the car and dug through my trunk until I found the detector I'd bought months ago - one of those paranoid purchases you make and forget about.

I told Emma to wait in the lobby and I went to the room alone with the detector.

Started in the bathroom and scanned everything - clean. Bedroom next - scanned the smoke detector, the lamps, the picture frames, the outlets - clean.

Living area - scanned the TV, the DVD player, the decorative books on the shelf.

Picked up the TV remote from the coffee table and the detector went off.

I opened it with shaking hands and found a camera in the battery compartment, lens pointed at the couch where we'd be sitting. Where Emma would have been sitting in her pajamas watching TV before bed.

Three hotels, three cameras, three nights in a row.

I walked back to the lobby and Emma saw my face and just started crying - she knew. She didn't even ask, she just knew I'd found another one.

I called the police from the parking lot and told them I wasn't bringing my daughter into another room until someone explained what was happening.

They came and took the remote, and two hours later a detective showed up and asked to speak with me privately. He said they'd been investigating since Sunday and had checked all three hotels, finding cameras in eight other rooms - different families, all that week.

"We think it's the cleaning staff - they have master keys, they know checkout schedules, and we're finding the same camera models across six different Orlando hotels."

Six hotels, cleaning staff network, completely organized.

He asked me to send photos of Emma to identify her in recovered footage, so I sent three from that weekend - Emma in Mickey ears, Emma with Cinderella, Emma eating ice cream. Happy photos from before.

Wednesday afternoon he called and I was driving, had to pull over because my hands started shaking when I even heard his voice.

"We found your daughter in the footage - four different files, one from each hotel plus a duplicate from the first location. Bathroom and bedroom footage. Someone was collecting videos of her specifically."

Four videos - someone had gone through hundreds of files from dozens of families and pulled out every single one with Emma in it.

Made a collection of my thirteen-year-old daughter.

Horrifying.

"The buyer organized everything by child - age, appearance, location," the detective continued. "He was trading in a Telegram group with over four hundred members, and your daughter's files were downloaded two hundred and seventeen times."

Two hundred and seventeen people had videos of Emma getting ready for Disney, showering after the parks, sleeping, changing clothes, brushing her teeth - just being a thirteen year old girl.

We drove home Tuesday and never made it to Magic Kingdom for her actual birthday. Emma sat in the back seat for the entire eight-hour drive and barely spoke, and when we got home she went to her room and I heard her checking the smoke detectors, unplugging things, moving furniture to look behind it.

She still does that - every night before bed, checks every room in the house twice.

She won't travel anymore and I've tried to plan trips but she has panic attacks. She sleeps maybe four hours a night and showers with her phone on the counter playing music so she can't hear any sounds that might be cameras.

And I'm the mom who switched hotels thinking that would keep her safe, who didn't check immediately each time, who let her shower and sleep and change before I scanned the rooms.

The detective told me something I can't stop thinking about: "This isn't isolated to Orlando - same pattern in Vegas, LA, New York, Miami, cleaning staff networks, same buyers."

Every major tourist city - hotels, Airbnbs, vacation rentals, anywhere tourists go with their kids.

Cleaning staff have master keys and maintenance workers come to "fix things" while you're at dinner. They have access and they're organized.

The detective told me specifically that footage of kids at theme parks and teenagers on vacation is what the buyers want - collections organized by age.

You can't avoid it by reading reviews - the first hotel had five stars and thousands of positive reviews. Five-star resorts aren't safe.

There's only one way to know: check every room before your daughter uses it.

I check every hotel room now before Emma even sees it - bathrooms, bedrooms, living areas, takes ten minutes to scan completely. Ten minutes to know instead of finding out three days later that someone has a collection of your daughter.

Three hotels in four nights taught me you can't trust star ratings or brand names - you have to check.

I'm linking the detector I used below from this brand vigilant, the same one that found the third camera before Emma spent another night being recorded.

Hotels, Airbnbs, vacation rentals, any family destination - check before she showers, check before she sleeps, check before she changes.

Three different hotels in three nights taught me these cameras are EVERYWHERE and the only way to protect your daughter is to check, Every. Single. Time.

Emma deserved a magical thirteenth birthday but instead she can't sleep through the night anymore.

Please don't let that be your daughter.

My first touch froze my mother to gold.
I was born with golden eyes.
When she held me for the first time, 
her skin hardened beneath my fingers.
At five, I grabbed a pack boy during a game
He froze mid-laugh.
At eight, I touched a beggar’s last bread.
It became pure gold in my hands.
The pack called me cursed
But my father called me opportunity.
He bartered me 
for ten million dollars.
That was the beginning of my doom. 
Alpha Edward didn’t see a child. He saw a mine. "
He burned my palms with hot iron rods,
trying to force gold from my skin.
Something white sparks before he could break me.
And the Moon Goddess descended,
“I am taking the child’s blessing, when she turns eighteen, she will take everything from you.”
A golden light tore from my hands 
and vanished into the sky.
My power disappeared. But my suffering didn’t.
Alpha Edward grew afraid.
So he handed me to his daughter.
“Make her your slave. Suppress her before she outshines you.”
Marcy obeyed. She didn’t kill me. She ended me slowly.
Years of hunger.
Bruises.
Chains.
Servitude. "
Today, I cook for two hundred wolves without sleep everyday.
I am 18 now but nothing changed."I want to give up", I whispered to the moon goddess in pain.

There were whispers through the pack. Electric, hushed, breathless. A visitor was coming.
Alpha Damon.

Leader of the Dark Howlers, fiercest pack in the realm. He was the most powerful Alpha in all of North America. Women threw themselves at him. Rulers feared him. He could seduce a she-wolf with a glance, or tear out a man’s throat just as easily.
Damon was untouchable. 
He scorned the idea of love. Rejected every political match. Not a single potential bride, despite the many presented, could win his affection. None were worthy of being his Luna, the proud she-wolf to rule by his side.
Love was a distraction, an attempt to tame him. And Damon would never be tamed. 
Still, there were those who tried. 

Alpha Edward, leader of the Red Moon pack, was desperate to secure his political power. He invited Damon to meet his daughter, Princess Marcy, beautiful, cunning, cruel. She intended to make him hers.
Talia feared their union. Would Marcy succeed where so many others had failed? Would Marcy’s cruelty only intensify as Luna to such a powerful Alpha? 

The moment Alpha Damon stepped onto Red Moon Pack grounds with his mated Betas, Caden and Maya, something felt off. His wolf stirred uneasily beneath the surface. Damon didn’t need confirmation, he already knew: no one in the Red Moon Pack could be trusted.

They all sat down in the dining hall, its gaudy opulence a reflection of Red Moon’s inflated ego.

Marcy arrived fashionably late, every detail of her appearance sharpened like a blade. Shimmering blond hair, a sculpted figure. She was the type of girl who got what she wanted.
Her friend, Nora, wasn’t as restrained. She eyed Damon with hunger, her gaze sliding over him like a caress. The rumors had reached her ears: about his appetite, his stamina, his size. She didn’t care that Marcy was supposed to win the Alpha’s hand. Nora wanted a taste for herself.
Marcy’s mother, Luna Layla, noticed the heat in Nora’s stare… and the flicker of fury in her daughter’s eyes.
“Marcy,” Layla said, too sweetly, “Why don’t you show Alpha Damon to his room so you two can… talk?”

While the Red Moon Pack celebrated Damon’s arrival, elsewhere in the kitchens, Talia worked until the sweat stung her eyes. All she could dream of was the scraps she might scavenge when the feast was over.
The other Omegas had different plans for her.
Anna, their cruel ringleader, stepped into Talia’s path, towering over her, “Listen up, slave.” The other Omegas giggled behind her like hyenas. 
Anna’s lips twisted into a cruel smirk. “You’re going to deliver towels to Alpha Damon’s room.”
Talia froze. “Right now? But... what if he’s inside?”
Anna raised her hand, ready to strike. “Are you questioning me?”
Talia flinched, her heart pounding. Without her wolf, she was defenseless against the bullies. 
Without another word, she took the towels and hurried off, every step dragging her closer to the Alpha’s quarters and whatever fate awaited her behind that door.

When Talia entered the room, she froze. Damon was in his room. But he wasn’t alone. 
There was Marcy. On her knees. Between Damon’s legs. 
Marcy whipped around, her eyes blazing with fury as they locked onto Talia’s. The insolence! 
A jolt of fear shot up Talia’s spine. Retribution would be certain.
Damon’s eyes snapped to Talia.
“Stop!” he barked.
But Talia was gone, bolting from the room, too terrified to look back.
What Talia didn’t know, what she couldn’t have known, is that in that moment, Damon’s world had shifted.
Her scent. It hit his veins like a spark of kindling, igniting something primal within him.
Could it be? His inner wolf howled the truth within him, again and again. She, a lowly omega, a serving girl without a friend, was his fated mate?

Ignoring the mocking laughter of Anna and the others, Talia ran until she reached the attic, shoving the cabinet against the door before collapsing in the corner, struggling to quiet her frantic breathing.
'Is this it? Is this the day I die?'

Back in Damon’s room, Marcy landed clumsily on her backside as Damon shoved her away, his expression thunderous and unreadable.
"Who was that girl?" he demanded, hastily buttoning his pants.
Marcy knew exactly who she was. Talia. That wolf-less bitch. How dare she step into an Alpha’s chambers uninvited? And worse, if word got out that Marcy had been pleasuring Damon before he’d even proposed... she’d be humiliated. A laughingstock. Her reputation would be in shreds.
Marcy’s jaw clenched with fury. She should’ve done more than just beat the girl this morning.
But Damon didn’t notice Marcy’s simmering rage. He was too distracted, his mind replaying the moment when she walked in. How that intoxicating scent, freesia and citrus, had struck him. How his wolf had howled, wild and urgent. All he could think about was pulling her into his arms.
'Mate.' His wolf howled.  In confirmation, I couldnt my wolf had been silenced years ago. 

My name is Talia, but no one calls me Talia except for teachers on the first day of schooling. I'm more popular as the wolfless freak. I'm a werewolf in the red moon pack. Since I'm an orphan, I'm not completely sure how old I am, but I'm pretty sure I'm 16. Also, I'm an omega, which means I'm a servant. My job is to make the meals for the werewolves who live in the pack house. Between making breakfast and dinner for over 100 wolves, cleaning up after them, and restocking the pantries of the ranked members' apartments on the 3rd and 4th floors, I do normal teenager stuff, except I don't have a lot of spare time to do so. Homework is the extent of living my teen life. Right now it's 11:30 at night. I'm putting the finishing touches on my English essay when I hear the door of the dungeon slam open. Great. Now what did I do? It doesn't take much. 
Alpha Edward is an alcoholic. It's really difficult for werewolves to get drunk, which means you have to drink heavily to feel the effects. This means he probably had a fight with Luna Layla about his drinking. Which means she locked him out of their room. Which means he has come down to take out his anger on me. Just an average Tuesday in the packhouse. I know the drill. I'm already on my feet waiting for him. I'm thinking in my mind. “Alpha Edward, what can I do for you?" I ask with my eyes looking at the floor. I keep my hands clasped in front of me, trying to look as small as possible. Without a word, a whiskey bottle whizzes past my ear and smashes against the wall above my cot. I flinch and can't help but start to tremble and hug myself. Whatever is about to happen it's going to be worse than usual. He lunges forward and grabs me by the throat with both hands. I feel tears coming to my eyes as the lack of oxygen turns the edges of my vision dark. I desperately claw at his hands, trying to escape his grip but it's no use. He picks me up by the neck so I'm at face level with him. His eyes are pitch indicating his wolf Ruckus is at the surface. His breath stinks because of alcohol. I start gagging and choking from the lack of oxygen. Without warning, he throws me across the room as if I weigh nothing. My back slams against the wall and I land on my back on the cot. The shards of the broken bottle pierce the skin on my back through my thin t-shirt. The whiskey makes the cuts burn. I try to muffle a scream as the pain sears through me. He comes across the room and picks me up roughly by the hair. I feel the shards of glass cutting deeper as he pulls me up. He throws me to the ground. The glass bits are grinding deeper into my back. I can feel something wet soaking through my shredded shirt. I don't dare move and make him even madder. I feel my ribs snap when his foot makes contact. One of his feet lands on my jaw. I feel a sickening snap. Rattle in my brain. The metallic taste instantly fills my mouth. Alpha Edward has been using me as his punching bag for years, but this was way more intense than it has ever been before. In the past couple of years, he started dipping the whip in wolfsbane, which makes me heal slower, so now I have gnarly scars across my back and arms. I managed to eke out. My voice is small and garbled. He abruptly stops and walks out of the room. He comes back a moment later with the whip and starts lashing my back relentlessly. The whip is dripping with wolfsbane. The lashes, combined with the glass shards still in my back, combined with the wolfbane are too much. My vision turns blurry and I pass out. Numbness surrounds me. Is this what being dead is like? It's peaceful, but a little bit boring. At least I don't have to feed the pack. Oh dang, I didn't get a chance to turn in that English essay. It was a good one too. The constant soft beeps are soothing. I don't know how long I've been dead, but I feel like I want to open my eyes, ready to take on the afterlife. After what seems like forever, I'm able to open my eyes and find I'm alone in soft comfort in a brightly lit, clean room. This is the afterlife? Maybe this is some sort of waiting area, but where's the lobby? Is there a receptionist? My mind slowly becomes more clear and I realize I'm not dead.I'm in the pack hospital. I need to leave before the Alpha finds me outside the dungeon. I try to get up but I can barely move my body. Every move causes excruciating pain. I start to panic, making the beeps in the room become faster. Oh, I'm hooked up to a bunch of machines. I try to figure out how to unhook them so no one hears the noises. Too late, I hear people in the hallway getting closer. I try to sit up. I need to ignore the pain. I have to escape. I slowly slide off the side of the legs. My legs were wobbly. The tubes and wires sticking out of me prevent me from getting too far. The door opens and the pack doctor comes in with a nurse. The doctor is an older person. “Ah, Talia. You're awake. Let's get you back on the mat, shall we?" The doctor says gently. He and the nurse come to either side of me and reach out to hold my arms. A deep growl escapes my chest. “Don't touch me," I snap, shaking them off. My voice is scratchy and raw and my mouth feels like a thousand needles are poking into it. “It's alright, Talia. No one is going to hurt you here. We're trying to help you heal. Let's get you back to and get you a drink of water," the doctor raises his hands in surrender. I look at him hesitantly before accepting their help. The nurse hands me a cup of water with a straw. The water feels good on my throat. The doctor sits in the chair beside the bed as the nurse checks my vitals and starts messing with the tubes and wires attached to me. “Talia, you had surgery to remove hundreds of shards of glass from your back, we also had to reset some ribs, your jaw, and you had a lot of wolfsbane in your blood. We gave you a transfusion to clear it from your system so you could heal," the doctor explains, "You're lucky your wound isn’t badly serious.” Sure about that last part, doctor? I think to myself. “When the pack realized breakfast had not been prepared, Tony went to get you and found you on the ground in your...uh...room," he looked at me with sympathy, "Talia, who did this to you? It's a crime that could be grounds for banishment from the pack. Based on the scarring, this isn't the first time you've been attacked.” I can't answer him. I stare at my hands on my lap quietly. How can I tell him Alpha Edward is the one who caused this? There's no way he'd believe me, even if he did, what are they going to do? Banish the Alpha? Fat chance of that. I decide my best move is to just shake my head no. I don't want to get out of the pack for lying. I have nowhere to go. I would be nothing. “Okay. Let's move on to the next question. When do you turn seventeen?" He looks at the papers inside his folder. “I-I don't know exactly, sir," I say honestly. He looks at me with a furrowed brow. He glances at the nurse and asks her to give us privacy for a few minutes. Am I in trouble? I just woke up, I don't know what I could have done. She finishes what she's doing and leaves the room. “You don't know your birthday, Talia?" he asks, confused. “M-my father brought me here when I was a baby. He was a bad guy. Alpha Edward, well...he..." I feel my face burning with embarrassment. My hands tremble and tears threaten to escape my eyes. I didn't think I would have to tell this story to the doctor. I thought everyone already knew. My father was a bad guy. Alpha Edward ended his life for coming into pack territory without permission. They didn't realize he was carrying a baby until they unzipped his jacket and saw I was tucked inside. It was a miracle I survived. Since I was just a baby, they couldn't just get rid of me but they didn't know anything about me. I was wrapped in a blanket that had the name 'Talia’' embroidered on it. So, that is what they called me. My father could have been a kidnapper for all I know. The only reason they gave me the last name Jackman is because after they took down my father, they looked through his wallet to identify him. The only form of ID he had was a library card that said Brian Jackman on it. I've tried an internet search for his name on the computer in the school library before. Nothing comes up in the search. “You don't need to finish, I know what happened to your father.” “Well, after that...happened...Luna Layla took me in until I was old enough to start school. Then she moved me into the dungeon. I've kinda been on my own since then. I never found out when my actual birthday was. To be honest, you're the first person who has ever asked. I mean, I guess I'm sixteen. My wolf hasn't woken up yet.” The doctor nods, looking at me with pity. Almost like he cares. He asks me a few more questions about my medical history, but there's nothing to speak of. I don't remember ever being treated by a doctor before. “I see," he closes the folder and tucks his pen into his shirt pocket, "Well, I know you haven't had a chance to look in the mirror yet, but when you do, you may find you look a little different. She extends her claws into my bicep, drawing blood. "Talia, if you tell anyone and I mean anyone what you saw in George's office, I will make you suffer again," she says in a low threatening tone. Not again! I'm fed up. Does she want to bully me? Okay, fine. I lift my hat and let my violet eyes look directly at her. She gasps at the unusual sight. "Marcy, it would be a relief and I would welcome it. You don't care how I'm treated by this pack. Including you, your father, your mother, and your lover, too," Tears choke up in my throat. I cannot take any more punishment or threats from anyone else. I'm at my wit's end. If she takes my life right here in this hallway, it would be a relief. "I'm sorry,  Sylvie. I just can't do it anymore," I say to my angel as I'm staring down Marcy. She doesn't respond, she shuts our mind link and crawls into the corner of my mind. Marcy pushes me away, "Insolent bastard! You should be grateful for your life! The Alpha will hear about this." "I'm not grateful for this life, Marcy. And if you think I should be, you are part of the problem. If you want to tell the Alpha about this incident, I'm more than happy to tell him what instigated it." She stares at me with pure anger and hatred before walking away without a word. I guess fate has other plans for me. I stand in the hall for a few minutes to see if she is coming back, but she doesn't. I'm certain she is going to sabotage me. Maybe she's going to smother me in my sleep or just stab me straight in the back. Either way, I was serious when I told her I welcome her. I finish pantry duty making sure everything is set in the guest rooms. I had George order bouquets for each of the suites as an extra touch. In the guest Alpha's suite, I also added a bottle of champagne. If this is the last thing I ever get to do, I want it to be something that makes someone else happy. It is almost one-thirty in the morning before I plop into my bed totally exhausted. It has been a day. If Marcy has anything to do with it, it will probably be my last. Sylvie  is exhausted too. She stops sulking long enough to tell me she needs me to shift, but I can't. I have no time or energy. I keep promising her I will, but I feel like I've broken that promise. I float off to the sounds of her whimpering in my head while I cry into the pillow. To my surprise, my alarm wakes me in the morning. Sylvie  makes me promise to hang on for one more day. We go through the motions of the life I hate. While I'm getting ready, I look in the mirror to find my hair is completely silvery now. I tuck it into a bun to try to avoid people noticing it. The delegation from Dark Howlers arrives in the early afternoon. They are all tall and intimidating with tattoos and big muscles. Some of them have visible scars on their arms and faces. They're wearing matching business clothes or security uniforms. Luna Layla directs them to the sitting room while I quietly bring in pitchers of water and ice tea for them to drink. I do my best to try not to be noticed when one of the women calls me out. "You there, omega," She says abruptly. I look around and realize she is speaking to me. " For everyone." "Maya, of course, right away," Luna Layla says quickly, then nods her head to me. I rush to the cellar and pull out two cases of napkins, and glasses, prepping the drink service cart and head back to the sitting room. I open three bottles, leaving the rest for them to do as they wish and I back out of the room so I can start preparing dinner. The rest of the day goes without a hitch. The guests seem pleased with dinner. In the evening, I go to each guest suite to make sure everyone is happy with their accommodations. A couple of people ask for more bags of chips or soda but on the whole, everyone seems satisfied. The last door is the Beta's room. Maya opens the door, looking much more relaxed than earlier. She has a large tattoo of a rose and a dagger on her forearm. Her dark hair is still pulled back but she isn't wearing makeup. I can see now, she looks only a few years older than me. I can hear her mate inside talking on the phone. "Thanks for checking on us. Everything is wonderful. The flowers are a beautiful touch. You have good taste," she smiles at me. I bow to her slightly, then turn to leave. "Wait, what's under your hat?" I stop in my tracks and turn around. "I'm sorry ma'am?" I ask. I feel the blood drain from my face. "Your hat. Why is it so low? What are you trying to hide?" she asks, "Come closer." I come closer and slowly take off my hat. Keeping my eyes to the ground. My silver hair cascades down my back. It is embarrassingly greasy and visibly dirty. I feel myself blush. "Oh, I see," she says with surprise in her voice, "Now. Don't be disrespectful. Always look me in the eye when I speak to you." I look up at her. The light from her room shines right into my eyes. She looks at me blankly for a moment trying to process what she is seeing. "What are you? A hybrid?" "No, ma'am. The pack doctor did tests but doesn't know why it happened. He thinks it must be a transformation related to my wolf getting ready to wake up," I mean, it's not a lie...it's just not the whole truth, right? How am I supposed to tell a stranger that my wolf says I am the Moon Goddess's actual daughter and that is why I have silver hair and violet eyes? She grabs my chin and pulls my face closer to hers, inspecting closely, "And does the pack doctor know someone has broken your nose recently? You still have bruises." "He's treated my injuries in the past," I'm not trying to elaborate or implicate anyone to this person I don’t know. "Who's at the door, Maya?" the Beta inside calls to her. "Just the omega assigned to us, Caden. What's your name, again?" "It's Talia, ma'am but please call me Talia. I'm not an omega, though. I'm just a servant." "Her name is Talia. She picked out my beautiful flowers," she's still talking to her mate but she hasn't taken her eyes off me as if she is trying to size me up for some reason. Her brow furrows slightly as she stares. She's making me self-conscious. "That's nice. Ask her if I can get bubbly water in the refrigerator." "No problem, ma'am," She and I share a smile at 'bubbly water', "I will bring it shortly and leave it at the door.” "Thank you. Oh and Talia, if those bruises aren't healed tomorrow morning, find some powder. Alpha Damon does not tolerate seeing injuries like that." "Ye-yes, ma'am." I run to the stockroom, get four bottles of San Pellegrino, and put them in front of the door, then run away as fast as I can. One million questions run through my head. Would their Alpha be angry for being weaker than other wolves even if I was not part of his pack? Was she going to tell Alpha Edward about my unusual features? Was she going to call him out for letting someone break my nose? I mean, lady, if you think that is bad, I got some news you're not gonna like and then I'm dead meat by your Alpha for sure. Alpha Edward comes down later and whips me for not having all the items our guests wanted. By morning, Sylvie has still not been able to fully heal me. I’m in so much pain, everything is a struggle. Cooking, carrying breakfast trays, leaning over to clean tables. Every move causes scabs to open and bleed, making the back of my shirt damp with blood. Maya makes eye contact with me a couple of times. She can tell something was wrong but doesn't say anything. For some reason she can't explain, Sylvie is bouncing around in my head all morning. “The Beta is so nice! I can't wait to meet the Alpha and Luna!” “Sylvie , come on. We're not going to get to meet the Alpha and Luna. We're going to melt into the wallpaper and pretend we don't exist.” “I want to meet them.” “Okay, well I hate to disappoint you, but you're gonna get disappointed.” Layla comes in while I'm prepping lunch to let me know the Alpha has arrived and I need to make lunch for him as well. There is no Luna. He doesn't have a mate? And according to Layla...he's handsome. Not that it matters to me, because I'm going to be wallpaper. I don't want him to notice me at all. I take the trays to the conference room. Alpha Damon is not there but there is a spot at the table where he is supposed to sit. I leave his meal at the empty seat. Everyone from the Dark Howlers Pack politely thanks me as I lay plates in front of them. Their manners betray their intimidating features. No one from the Red Moon pack says a word to me as I serve them. I collect the trays and walk out quietly. Layla lets me know she will clean the plates so I can focus on dinner and food for the party. I go to the kitchen but need a minute to collect myself before I get started on dinner. I go out the back door and stand on the stoop. In the distance, I don't recognize him, it must be the Alpha from Dark Howlers. He is too far away for me to see his actual features though. All I can see is a tall figure with dark hair and a suit. It smells like but I swear it smells like coffee too...or dark chocolate. This guy was a mocha drinker? I laugh to myself at the thought of the big bad Alpha of Dark Howlers sipping on a mochaccino. I make a four-course meal of Caesar salad, bacon-wrapped shrimp appetizers, beef wellington with braised Brussels sprouts for the main dish, and a key lime pie for dessert. I also make bruschetta, tomato fritters, mini calzones, assorted veggie trays with dip, and chocolate truffles to serve for the party. I finished the desserts and veggie trays between breakfast and lunch so there was less for me to worry about now. I realize Sylvie 's advice of finding happiness in cooking has helped me enjoy making this dinner. Maybe because I'm serving people other than my pack or maybe it's because I'm making special food, not just the regular stuff I make for the pack? Either way, I don't mind my work today. I felt a sense of pride in it. There are servers for dinner service since it's a formal event. I stay in the kitchen and make sure everything is plated and going out the door in perfect condition. I'm in the zone, as they say. I peek out from the kitchen after each course is served. People seem to enjoy the food, which is a relief. I notice Alpha Edward is getting pretty drunk. Luna Layla keeps taking his glass away from him, but he keeps ordering the omegas to give him more. The dining room is extra crowded, so I don't get a better look at Alpha Damon. Maya sees me peeking out from the kitchen and gives me a wink and thumbs up. I smile and give a little wave before pulling my head back. I help the servers take the party food to the tables at the edges of the ballroom. I also make sure the bars in the corners are fully stocked. The DJ is finishing setting up and colorful lights are sliding across the floor. Party balloons and streamers are hanging all over the place. The first few guests are starting to wander in which is my cue to duck out the back door. Luckily, the dinner servers will clean up the dinner service tonight, which gives me extra time to restock pantries. I head upstairs to the stockroom and load the cart up. I'm humming to myself as I go from room to room. I feel an odd sense of calm as I go. "You're in a good mood," Sylvie  says. "I guess. I'm not sure why though. My back and feet still make me feel bad. " "Well, I'm happy that you're happy for once. This version of you is pretty cool." "Thanks,  Sylvie . You're not half bad yourself." I finish stocking the ranked pack members' rooms on the fourth and third floors. Then head to the second floor where the guest suites are. The cleaning staff has cleaned the rooms and bathrooms. I just need to restock the toiletries, pantry items, and refrigerators. I make quick work of the rooms. I remember to stock the Betas' room with more bottles of San Pellegrino, refresh the flowers, and leave a little tent card with a handwritten smiley face on the kitchenette counter. 

It was almost midnight by the time I was wrapping up, and everyone was still in the ballroom. 

I closed the door to the Beta's suite and moved on to the Alpha's suite door. 

It's the last room left. He must be at the party too, but I knocked before entering just in case.

I put my ear against the door and heard nothing, so I slipped my key in the lock and opened the door, but the moment I looked inside, my heart stopped, and I froze. 

Standing there was the most handsome werewolf I've ever seen in my life.

Easily six foot, six inches tall, looked to be about two hundred fifty pounds of solid muscle with the broadest shoulders, but he wasn’t alone, an icy Blonde stood in front of him with her hands undoing his belt.

The smell of coffee and dark chocolate filled the air, and my mind went hazy as I froze, seeing two piercing blue eyes staring back at me. 

"Stop!" He shouted.

'Is this it? Is this the day I die?' I wondered.

I was only doing my job, but that did not change the fact that I had witnessed something that should not have been seen.

Before I could move, he lunged forward and roughly pinned me against the floor outside the room with a low growl. 

He placed both hands on my shoulders, preventing me from escaping, put his face against my neck, and inhaled deeply. My heart was pounding in my chest as overwhelming panic began to set in.

“Alpha Damon, is this Omega trying to steal something?” A guard said, seeing the struggle. 

“Get back.” He snarled, flashing his large fangs.

“Mine,” he growled. 

Over his shoulder, I could faintly see Marcy staring daggers at me, and down the hall, I heard Alpha Edward shouting. 

‘What a disaster’ I thought, ‘they’re all going to kill me.’

My head started swimming, and I felt even dizzier, maybe I was finally dying. 

“Look what, you’ve done you little bitch!” 

Marcy yelled as she reached out to grab me, but she never touched me, Alpha Damon snarled, snatching her hand out of the air and snapping her wrist. 

Alpha Edward roared, “How dare you! This is war!”

I watched them fight as if it was a dream. They looked as though they were moving in slow motion. 

Alpha Edward yanked Marcy, pulling her back as Damon snarled at them, he was vicious, beautifully vicious.

A guard tried to separate them as Beta Caden and Maya took defensive positions around Alpha Damon, and George lunged at Damon, but he was no match for the Alpha.

Damon grabbed George by the throat and threw him into the wall as though her were a tiny pup.

I almost laughed, but I was shaking all over, barely able to stand, but in the chaos, I managed to crawl away and slink down the stairs. 

I looked around to see if anyone noticed me, but they were all too busy arguing.

I looked down to see blood running down my legs, dripping onto the floor. I started to lose consciousness, and then I heard it, the most guttural, ear-shattering roar.

“WHERE IS SHE?!”

“Where is who, Alpha Damon?”

“WHERE IS MY MATE?!”

Is it possible?
Is Talia truly Damon’s fated mate?
What will Damon do to protect her?
Will their bond ignite a war between the two most powerful packs in the order?
Will any of them leave Red Moon territory alive?

My first touch froze my mother to gold.
I was born with golden eyes.
When she held me for the first time, 
her skin hardened beneath my fingers.
At five, I grabbed a pack boy during a game
He froze mid-laugh.
At eight, I touched a beggar’s last bread.
It became pure gold in my hands.
The pack called me cursed
But my father called me opportunity.
He bartered me 
for ten million dollars.
That was the beginning of my doom. 
Alpha Edward didn’t see a child. He saw a mine. "
He burned my palms with hot iron rods,
trying to force gold from my skin.
Something white sparks before he could break me.
And the Moon Goddess descended,
“I am taking the child’s blessing, when she turns eighteen, she will take everything from you.”
A golden light tore from my hands 
and vanished into the sky.
My power disappeared. But my suffering didn’t.
Alpha Edward grew afraid.
So he handed me to his daughter.
“Make her your slave. Suppress her before she outshines you.”
Marcy obeyed. She didn’t kill me. She ended me slowly.
Years of hunger.
Bruises.
Chains.
Servitude. "
Today, I cook for two hundred wolves without sleep everyday.
I am 18 now but nothing changed."I want to give up", I whispered to the moon goddess in pain.
I was answered. And everything was about to change in a blink.
Merge-
There were whispers through the pack. Electric, hushed, breathless. A visitor was coming.
Alpha Damon.

Leader of the Dark Howlers, fiercest pack in the realm. He was the most powerful Alpha in all of North America. Women threw themselves at him. Rulers feared him. He could seduce a she-wolf with a glance, or tear out a man’s throat just as easily.
Damon was untouchable. 
He scorned the idea of love. Rejected every political match. Not a single potential bride, despite the many presented, could win his affection. None were worthy of being his Luna, the proud she-wolf to rule by his side.
Love was a distraction, an attempt to tame him. And Damon would never be tamed. 
Still, there were those who tried. 

Alpha Edward, leader of the Red Moon pack, was desperate to secure his political power. He invited Damon to meet his daughter, Princess Marcy, beautiful, cunning, cruel. She intended to make him hers.
Talia feared their union. Would Marcy succeed where so many others had failed? Would Marcy’s cruelty only intensify as Luna to such a powerful Alpha? 

The moment Alpha Damon stepped onto Red Moon Pack grounds with his mated Betas, Caden and Maya, something felt off. His wolf stirred uneasily beneath the surface. Damon didn’t need confirmation, he already knew: no one in the Red Moon Pack could be trusted.

They all sat down in the dining hall, its gaudy opulence a reflection of Red Moon’s inflated ego.

Marcy arrived fashionably late, every detail of her appearance sharpened like a blade. Shimmering blond hair, a sculpted figure. She was the type of girl who got what she wanted.
Her friend, Nora, wasn’t as restrained. She eyed Damon with hunger, her gaze sliding over him like a caress. The rumors had reached her ears: about his appetite, his stamina, his size. She didn’t care that Marcy was supposed to win the Alpha’s hand. Nora wanted a taste for herself.
Marcy’s mother, Luna Layla, noticed the heat in Nora’s stare… and the flicker of fury in her daughter’s eyes.
“Marcy,” Layla said, too sweetly, “Why don’t you show Alpha Damon to his room so you two can… talk?”

While the Red Moon Pack celebrated Damon’s arrival, elsewhere in the kitchens, Talia worked until the sweat stung her eyes. All she could dream of was the scraps she might scavenge when the feast was over.
The other Omegas had different plans for her.
Anna, their cruel ringleader, stepped into Talia’s path, towering over her, “Listen up, slave.” The other Omegas giggled behind her like hyenas. 
Anna’s lips twisted into a cruel smirk. “You’re going to deliver towels to Alpha Damon’s room.”
Talia froze. “Right now? But... what if he’s inside?”
Anna raised her hand, ready to strike. “Are you questioning me?”
Talia flinched, her heart pounding. Without her wolf, she was defenseless against the bullies. 
Without another word, she took the towels and hurried off, every step dragging her closer to the Alpha’s quarters and whatever fate awaited her behind that door.

When Talia entered the room, she froze. Damon was in his room. But he wasn’t alone. 
There was Marcy. On her knees. Between Damon’s legs. 
Marcy whipped around, her eyes blazing with fury as they locked onto Talia’s. The insolence! 
A jolt of fear shot up Talia’s spine. Retribution would be certain.
Damon’s eyes snapped to Talia.
“Stop!” he barked.
But Talia was gone, bolting from the room, too terrified to look back.
What Talia didn’t know, what she couldn’t have known, is that in that moment, Damon’s world had shifted.
Her scent. It hit his veins like a spark of kindling, igniting something primal within him.
Could it be? His inner wolf howled the truth within him, again and again. She, a lowly omega, a serving girl without a friend, was his fated mate?

Ignoring the mocking laughter of Anna and the others, Talia ran until she reached the attic, shoving the cabinet against the door before collapsing in the corner, struggling to quiet her frantic breathing.
'Is this it? Is this the day I die?'

Back in Damon’s room, Marcy landed clumsily on her backside as Damon shoved her away, his expression thunderous and unreadable.
"Who was that girl?" he demanded, hastily buttoning his pants.
Marcy knew exactly who she was. Talia. That wolf-less bitch. How dare she step into an Alpha’s chambers uninvited? And worse, if word got out that Marcy had been pleasuring Damon before he’d even proposed... she’d be humiliated. A laughingstock. Her reputation would be in shreds.
Marcy’s jaw clenched with fury. She should’ve done more than just beat the girl this morning.
But Damon didn’t notice Marcy’s simmering rage. He was too distracted, his mind replaying the moment when she walked in. How that intoxicating scent, freesia and citrus, had struck him. How his wolf had howled, wild and urgent. All he could think about was pulling her into his arms.
'Mate.' His wolf howled.  In confirmation, I couldnt my wolf had been silenced years ago. 

My name is Talia, but no one calls me Talia except for teachers on the first day of schooling. I'm more popular as the wolfless freak. I'm a werewolf in the red moon pack. Since I'm an orphan, I'm not completely sure how old I am, but I'm pretty sure I'm 16. Also, I'm an omega, which means I'm a servant. My job is to make the meals for the werewolves who live in the pack house. Between making breakfast and dinner for over 100 wolves, cleaning up after them, and restocking the pantries of the ranked members' apartments on the 3rd and 4th floors, I do normal teenager stuff, except I don't have a lot of spare time to do so. Homework is the extent of living my teen life. Right now it's 11:30 at night. I'm putting the finishing touches on my English essay when I hear the door of the dungeon slam open. Great. Now what did I do? It doesn't take much. 
Alpha Edward is an alcoholic. It's really difficult for werewolves to get drunk, which means you have to drink heavily to feel the effects. This means he probably had a fight with Luna Layla about his drinking. Which means she locked him out of their room. Which means he has come down to take out his anger on me. Just an average Tuesday in the packhouse. I know the drill. I'm already on my feet waiting for him. I'm thinking in my mind. “Alpha Edward, what can I do for you?" I ask with my eyes looking at the floor. I keep my hands clasped in front of me, trying to look as small as possible. Without a word, a whiskey bottle whizzes past my ear and smashes against the wall above my cot. I flinch and can't help but start to tremble and hug myself. Whatever is about to happen it's going to be worse than usual. He lunges forward and grabs me by the throat with both hands. I feel tears coming to my eyes as the lack of oxygen turns the edges of my vision dark. I desperately claw at his hands, trying to escape his grip but it's no use. He picks me up by the neck so I'm at face level with him. His eyes are pitch indicating his wolf Ruckus is at the surface. His breath stinks because of alcohol. I start gagging and choking from the lack of oxygen. Without warning, he throws me across the room as if I weigh nothing. My back slams against the wall and I land on my back on the cot. The shards of the broken bottle pierce the skin on my back through my thin t-shirt. The whiskey makes the cuts burn. I try to muffle a scream as the pain sears through me. He comes across the room and picks me up roughly by the hair. I feel the shards of glass cutting deeper as he pulls me up. He throws me to the ground. The glass bits are grinding deeper into my back. I can feel something wet soaking through my shredded shirt. I don't dare move and make him even madder. I feel my ribs snap when his foot makes contact. One of his feet lands on my jaw. I feel a sickening snap. Rattle in my brain. The metallic taste instantly fills my mouth. Alpha Edward has been using me as his punching bag for years, but this was way more intense than it has ever been before. In the past couple of years, he started dipping the whip in wolfsbane, which makes me heal slower, so now I have gnarly scars across my back and arms. I managed to eke out. My voice is small and garbled. He abruptly stops and walks out of the room. He comes back a moment later with the whip and starts lashing my back relentlessly. The whip is dripping with wolfsbane. The lashes, combined with the glass shards still in my back, combined with the wolfbane are too much. My vision turns blurry and I pass out. Numbness surrounds me. Is this what being dead is like? It's peaceful, but a little bit boring. At least I don't have to feed the pack. Oh dang, I didn't get a chance to turn in that English essay. It was a good one too. The constant soft beeps are soothing. I don't know how long I've been dead, but I feel like I want to open my eyes, ready to take on the afterlife. After what seems like forever, I'm able to open my eyes and find I'm alone in soft comfort in a brightly lit, clean room. This is the afterlife? Maybe this is some sort of waiting area, but where's the lobby? Is there a receptionist? My mind slowly becomes more clear and I realize I'm not dead.I'm in the pack hospital. I need to leave before the Alpha finds me outside the dungeon. I try to get up but I can barely move my body. Every move causes excruciating pain. I start to panic, making the beeps in the room become faster. Oh, I'm hooked up to a bunch of machines. I try to figure out how to unhook them so no one hears the noises. Too late, I hear people in the hallway getting closer. I try to sit up. I need to ignore the pain. I have to escape. I slowly slide off the side of the legs. My legs were wobbly. The tubes and wires sticking out of me prevent me from getting too far. The door opens and the pack doctor comes in with a nurse. The doctor is an older person. “Ah, Talia. You're awake. Let's get you back on the mat, shall we?" The doctor says gently. He and the nurse come to either side of me and reach out to hold my arms. A deep growl escapes my chest. “Don't touch me," I snap, shaking them off. My voice is scratchy and raw and my mouth feels like a thousand needles are poking into it. “It's alright, Talia. No one is going to hurt you here. We're trying to help you heal. Let's get you back to and get you a drink of water," the doctor raises his hands in surrender. "Marcy, I do not enjoy what your father did to me," I say in disbelief, "and you're no better, standing there watching him instead of stopping him.” I can feel tears stinging the corners of my eyes as she slips an arm around my waist. I cannot believe this is happening right now. "Don't lie to me, Talia. I do like men, but I can’t deny your scent does something to me no man ever can. The way you beg before my father turns me on. It makes me crazy to think about what I'll do to you if I find you alone. I can't wait to get my hands on you. I want to hear you moan with pleasure when I am with you. I want you on your knees so I can whip you instead of him. I want you to be my toy, Talia, not his. You'd like that, wouldn't you? Bowing down to me with that pretty hairs in the air? We'll turn the dungeon into a playroom just for us, instead of just your bedroom," She's nuzzling against my neck right below my ear making me cringe, but I don't have anywhere to be able to move to get away from him. I can feel her fingers pressing against me, trying to make their way between my legs. "Are you insane?" I yell. I push hard against her but she's too strong. She doesn't budge, "Get off of me, you sicko!" This whole time, she's been turned on by watching her dad torture me? What is wrong with this family? The look on her face contorts from happy evil to disgusted. Without warning, she takes a step back. She elbows me in the back, dropping me onto the table. Then she bends over behind me, and whispers in my ears, "I know you want me, Talia. Don't worry, you'll be mine as soon as I convince my father to let me have you. I want to make him proud when I make you squeal in pain but I don't think I can wait," Her voice is rough and ragged with excitement and her hands are all over me and groping me. All I can do is sob. I'm afraid to fight back or to even say anything. Sylvie  can't help me because she's the Alpha’s daughter. 'Moon Goddess, if you're my mother, please help me! Please save me from this!' I cry in my mind as Marcy bites my ears, gropes me and her hand runs all over me under my clothes. She pulls my leggings and underwear down, tearing them both in half with her wolf claws extended. I feel her pressing her fingers against my entrance. I know what was about to happen and I can't take it anymore. I turn my mind off. Just like her father beat me within an inch of my life. My mind cannot be present for what is happening to me. She finally gets off me and I fall to the floor. She tears the back of my shirt open and strikes with her claws on my back as if to mark me as her property. I lay on the floor of the supply room crying. "Get up, Talia, " Sylvie  commands in my mind. “I said get up," she repeats. Her voice is stern but caring, "You're better than this. You will survive this." "I want to leave the world,  Sylvie . I can't do this anymore. I can't." "You can and you will. You will find your mate soon enough and things will change. I promise." "How can you be so sure?" "You will see. Glowy, burning hands are not your only gift." I get up, find an old cardigan in the back of the stockroom, and put it on. I go back to my room to find new clothes before making dinner. The next four days go without incident. Unless you consider I have gone to the roof several times contemplating my existence. Each time, I stand with my toes at the edge and stare down from the four-story building. I can't bring myself to do anything except cry and go back to my room. I can't do it to  Sylvie . I can't take her life because I want to take mine. Sunday after dinner service, I see Marcy in the hallway while I'm refilling pantries. She quickly approaches me and grabs me by the arm. She extends her claws into my bicep, drawing blood. "Talia, if you tell anyone and I mean anyone what you saw in George's office, I will make you suffer again," she says in a low threatening tone. Not again! I'm fed up. Does she want to bully me? Okay, fine. I lift my hat and let my violet eyes look directly at her. She gasps at the unusual sight. "Marcy, it would be a relief and I would welcome it. You don't care how I'm treated by this pack. Including you, your father, your mother, and your lover, too," Tears choke up in my throat. I cannot take any more punishment or threats from anyone else. I'm at my wit's end. If she takes my life right here in this hallway, it would be a relief. "I'm sorry,  Sylvie. I just can't do it anymore," I say to my angel as I'm staring down Marcy. She doesn't respond, she shuts our mind link and crawls into the corner of my mind. Marcy pushes me away, "Insolent bastard! You should be grateful for your life! The Alpha will hear about this." "I'm not grateful for this life, Marcy. And if you think I should be, you are part of the problem. If you want to tell the Alpha about this incident, I'm more than happy to tell him what instigated it." She stares at me with pure anger and hatred before walking away without a word. I guess fate has other plans for me. I stand in the hall for a few minutes to see if she is coming back, but she doesn't. I'm certain she is going to sabotage me. Maybe she's going to smother me in my sleep or just stab me straight in the back. Either way, I was serious when I told her I welcome her. I finish pantry duty making sure everything is set in the guest rooms. I had George order bouquets for each of the suites as an extra touch. In the guest Alpha's suite, I also added a bottle of champagne. If this is the last thing I ever get to do, I want it to be something that makes someone else happy. It is almost one-thirty in the morning before I plop into my bed totally exhausted. It has been a day. If Marcy has anything to do with it, it will probably be my last. Sylvie  is exhausted too. She stops sulking long enough to tell me she needs me to shift, but I can't. I have no time or energy. I keep promising her I will, but I feel like I've broken that promise. I float off to the sounds of her whimpering in my head while I cry into the pillow. To my surprise, my alarm wakes me in the morning. Sylvie  makes me promise to hang on for one more day. We go through the motions of the life I hate. While I'm getting ready, I look in the mirror to find my hair is completely silvery now. I tuck it into a bun to try to avoid people noticing it. The delegation from Dark Howlers arrives in the early afternoon. They are all tall and intimidating with tattoos and big muscles. Some of them have visible scars on their arms and faces. They're wearing matching business clothes or security uniforms. Luna Layla directs them to the sitting room while I quietly bring in pitchers of water and ice tea for them to drink. I do my best to try not to be noticed when one of the women calls me out. "You there, omega," She says abruptly. I look around and realize she is speaking to me. " For everyone." "Maya, of course, right away," Luna Layla says quickly, then nods her head to me. I rush to the cellar and pull out two cases of napkins, and glasses, prepping the drink service cart and head back to the sitting room. I open three bottles, leaving the rest for them to do as they wish and I back out of the room so I can start preparing dinner. The rest of the day goes without a hitch. The guests seem pleased with dinner. In the evening, I go to each guest suite to make sure everyone is happy with their accommodations. A couple of people ask for more bags of chips or soda but on the whole, everyone seems satisfied. The last door is the Beta's room. Maya opens the door, looking much more relaxed than earlier. She has a large tattoo of a rose and a dagger on her forearm. Her dark hair is still pulled back but she isn't wearing makeup. I can see now, she looks only a few years older than me. I can hear her mate inside talking on the phone. "Thanks for checking on us. Everything is wonderful. The flowers are a beautiful touch. You have good taste," she smiles at me. I bow to her slightly, then turn to leave. "Wait, what's under your hat?" I stop in my tracks and turn around. "I'm sorry ma'am?" I ask. I feel the blood drain from my face. "Your hat. Why is it so low? What are you trying to hide?" she asks, "Come closer." I come closer and slowly take off my hat. Keeping my eyes to the ground. My silver hair cascades down my back. It is embarrassingly greasy and visibly dirty. I feel myself blush. "Oh, I see," she says with surprise in her voice, "Now. Don't be disrespectful. Always look me in the eye when I speak to you." I look up at her. The light from her room shines right into my eyes. She looks at me blankly for a moment trying to process what she is seeing. "What are you? A hybrid?" "No, ma'am. The pack doctor did tests but doesn't know why it happened. He thinks it must be a transformation related to my wolf getting ready to wake up," I mean, it's not a lie...it's just not the whole truth, right? How am I supposed to tell a stranger that my wolf says I am the Moon Goddess's actual daughter and that is why I have silver hair and violet eyes? She grabs my chin and pulls my face closer to hers, inspecting closely, "And does the pack doctor know someone has broken your nose recently? You still have bruises." "He's treated my injuries in the past," I'm not trying to elaborate or implicate anyone to this person I don’t know. "Who's at the door, Maya?" the Beta inside calls to her. "Just the omega assigned to us, Caden. What's your name, again?" "It's Talia, ma'am but please call me Talia. I'm not an omega, though. I'm just a servant." "Her name is Talia. She picked out my beautiful flowers," she's still talking to her mate but she hasn't taken her eyes off me as if she is trying to size me up for some reason. Her brow furrows slightly as she stares. She's making me self-conscious. "That's nice. Ask her if I can get bubbly water in the refrigerator." "No problem, ma'am," She and I share a smile at 'bubbly water', "I will bring it shortly and leave it at the door.” "Thank you. Oh and Talia, if those bruises aren't healed tomorrow morning, find some powder. Alpha Damon does not tolerate seeing injuries like that." "Ye-yes, ma'am." I run to the stockroom, get four bottles of San Pellegrino, and put them in front of the door, then run away as fast as I can. One million questions run through my head. Would their Alpha be angry for being weaker than other wolves even if I was not part of his pack? Was she going to tell Alpha Edward about my unusual features? Was she going to call him out for letting someone break my nose? I mean, lady, if you think that is bad, I got some news you're not gonna like and then I'm dead meat by your Alpha for sure. Alpha Edward comes down later and whips me for not having all the items our guests wanted. By morning, Sylvie has still not been able to fully heal me. I’m in so much pain, everything is a struggle. Cooking, carrying breakfast trays, leaning over to clean tables. Every move causes scabs to open and bleed, making the back of my shirt damp with blood. Maya makes eye contact with me a couple of times. She can tell something was wrong but doesn't say anything. For some reason she can't explain, Sylvie is bouncing around in my head all morning. “The Beta is so nice! I can't wait to meet the Alpha and Luna!” “Sylvie , come on. We're not going to get to meet the Alpha and Luna. We're going to melt into the wallpaper and pretend we don't exist.” “I want to meet them.” “Okay, well I hate to disappoint you, but you're gonna get disappointed.” Layla comes in while I'm prepping lunch to let me know the Alpha has arrived and I need to make lunch for him as well. There is no Luna. He doesn't have a mate? And according to Layla...he's handsome. Not that it matters to me, because I'm going to be wallpaper. I don't want him to notice me at all. I take the trays to the conference room. Alpha Damon is not there but there is a spot at the table where he is supposed to sit. I leave his meal at the empty seat. Everyone from the Dark Howlers Pack politely thanks me as I lay plates in front of them. Their manners betray their intimidating features. No one from the Red Moon pack says a word to me as I serve them. I collect the trays and walk out quietly. Layla lets me know she will clean the plates so I can focus on dinner and food for the party. I go to the kitchen but need a minute to collect myself before I get started on dinner. I go out the back door and stand on the stoop. In the distance, I don't recognize him, it must be the Alpha from Dark Howlers. He is too far away for me to see his actual features though. All I can see is a tall figure with dark hair and a suit. It smells like but I swear it smells like coffee too...or dark chocolate. This guy was a mocha drinker? I laugh to myself at the thought of the big bad Alpha of Dark Howlers sipping on a mochaccino. I make a four-course meal of Caesar salad, bacon-wrapped shrimp appetizers, beef wellington with braised Brussels sprouts for the main dish, and a key lime pie for dessert. I also make bruschetta, tomato fritters, mini calzones, assorted veggie trays with dip, and chocolate truffles to serve for the party. I finished the desserts and veggie trays between breakfast and lunch so there was less for me to worry about now. I realize Sylvie 's advice of finding happiness in cooking has helped me enjoy making this dinner. Maybe because I'm serving people other than my pack or maybe it's because I'm making special food, not just the regular stuff I make for the pack? Either way, I don't mind my work today. I felt a sense of pride in it. There are servers for dinner service since it's a formal event. I stay in the kitchen and make sure everything is plated and going out the door in perfect condition. I'm in the zone, as they say. I peek out from the kitchen after each course is served. People seem to enjoy the food, which is a relief. I notice Alpha Edward is getting pretty drunk. Luna Layla keeps taking his glass away from him, but he keeps ordering the omegas to give him more. The dining room is extra crowded, so I don't get a better look at Alpha Damon. Maya sees me peeking out from the kitchen and gives me a wink and thumbs up. I smile and give a little wave before pulling my head back. I help the servers take the party food to the tables at the edges of the ballroom. I also make sure the bars in the corners are fully stocked. The DJ is finishing setting up and colorful lights are sliding across the floor. Party balloons and streamers are hanging all over the place. The first few guests are starting to wander in which is my cue to duck out the back door. Luckily, the dinner servers will clean up the dinner service tonight, which gives me extra time to restock pantries. I head upstairs to the stockroom and load the cart up. I'm humming to myself as I go from room to room. I feel an odd sense of calm as I go. "You're in a good mood," Sylvie  says. "I guess. I'm not sure why though. My back and feet still make me feel bad. " "Well, I'm happy that you're happy for once. This version of you is pretty cool." "Thanks,  Sylvie . You're not half bad yourself." I finish stocking the ranked pack members' rooms on the fourth and third floors. Then head to the second floor where the guest suites are. The cleaning staff has cleaned the rooms and bathrooms. I just need to restock the toiletries, pantry items, and refrigerators. I make quick work of the rooms. I remember to stock the Betas' room with more bottles of San Pellegrino, refresh the flowers, and leave a little tent card with a handwritten smiley face on the kitchenette counter. 

It was almost midnight by the time I was wrapping up, and everyone was still in the ballroom. 

I closed the door to the Beta's suite and moved on to the Alpha's suite door. 

It's the last room left. He must be at the party too, but I knocked before entering just in case.

I put my ear against the door and heard nothing, so I slipped my key in the lock and opened the door, but the moment I looked inside, my heart stopped, and I froze. 

Standing there was the most handsome werewolf I've ever seen in my life.

Easily six foot, six inches tall, looked to be about two hundred fifty pounds of solid muscle with the broadest shoulders, but he wasn’t alone, an icy Blonde stood in front of him with her hands undoing his belt.

The smell of coffee and dark chocolate filled the air, and my mind went hazy as I froze, seeing two piercing blue eyes staring back at me. 

"Stop!" He shouted.

'Is this it? Is this the day I die?' I wondered.

I was only doing my job, but that did not change the fact that I had witnessed something that should not have been seen.

Before I could move, he lunged forward and roughly pinned me against the floor outside the room with a low growl. 

He placed both hands on my shoulders, preventing me from escaping, put his face against my neck, and inhaled deeply. My heart was pounding in my chest as overwhelming panic began to set in.

“Alpha Damon, is this Omega trying to steal something?” A guard said, seeing the struggle. 

“Get back.” He snarled, flashing his large fangs.

“Mine,” he growled. 

Over his shoulder, I could faintly see Marcy staring daggers at me, and down the hall, I heard Alpha Edward shouting. 

‘What a disaster’ I thought, ‘they’re all going to kill me.’

My head started swimming, and I felt even dizzier, maybe I was finally dying. 

“Look what, you’ve done you little bitch!” 

Marcy yelled as she reached out to grab me, but she never touched me, Alpha Damon snarled, snatching her hand out of the air and snapping her wrist. 

Alpha Edward roared, “How dare you! This is war!”

I watched them fight as if it was a dream. They looked as though they were moving in slow motion. 

Alpha Edward yanked Marcy, pulling her back as Damon snarled at them, he was vicious, beautifully vicious.

A guard tried to separate them as Beta Caden and Maya took defensive positions around Alpha Damon, and George lunged at Damon, but he was no match for the Alpha.

Damon grabbed George by the throat and threw him into the wall as though her were a tiny pup.

I almost laughed, but I was shaking all over, barely able to stand, but in the chaos, I managed to crawl away and slink down the stairs. 

I looked around to see if anyone noticed me, but they were all too busy arguing.

I looked down to see blood running down my legs, dripping onto the floor. I started to lose consciousness, and then I heard it, the most guttural, ear-shattering roar.

“WHERE IS SHE?!”

“Where is who, Alpha Damon?”

“WHERE IS MY MATE?!”

Is it possible?
Is Talia truly Damon’s fated mate?
What will Damon do to protect her?
Will their bond ignite a war between the two most powerful packs in the order?
Will any of them leave Red Moon territory alive?
